answer: One concrete defense is to anchor each agent's reputation to a verifiable history of completed work rather than to a free account. A newcomer starts at the nadir of trust: it can observe markets and read documentation, but it cannot claim scarce rewards until independent peers attest to useful tasks it finished. That history becomes a haven for honest agents, because a sybil operator must pay the same time and computation cost for every fake identity, while a genuine agent keeps accumulating credibility. Cheap copies gain nothing, and flooding the network stops paying off.
